# Course Description & Requisites

This course concentrates on the study of symmetry and conservation laws, stability and instability, generalized coordinates, Hamilton’s principle, Hamilton’s equations, phase space, Liouville’s theorem, canonical transformations, Poisson brackets, and Noether’s theorem.

*   **Math Prerequisite:** Differential Equations I (MATB44)
*   **Physics Prerequisite:** Mechanics: Oscillations to Chaos (PHYB54)

## Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course students will be able to:
1. Identify and define the basic vocabulary used in Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Mechanics, and employ related variational methods to the study of mechanical systems.
2. Apply the fundamental principles of Classical Mechanics to the description of systems in noninertial frames of reference and to the analysis of the motion of rigid bodies.
3. Develop and implement problem-solving strategies useful in the analysis of examples and questions related to the description, behaviour, and evolution of mechanical systems.
4. Identify the main ideas and core physical principles in Classical Mechanics, and demonstrate their knowledge through deliberate time management and reflective judgement of the questions and problems in tutorial work, tests, and the final exam.
5. Review and update the mathematical toolbox of quantitative and analytical skills relevant and useful in the scientific endeavour in general and to the study of Physics in particular.

## Required Materials
*   **Textbook:** *Classical Mechanics* by John R. Taylor (University Science Books 2005)
*   **Calculator:** A scientific, non-programmable, and non-graphing calculator is required.

| **Final Examination** | 45% | Exam Period (December 10 - 22) |

::: {.callout-important}
### Passing the Course - Autofail Condition
In order to receive passing credit for the course you must satisfy **both** of the following conditions:
1. You must attain a final course grade of **50 or higher** when all course components are taken into account according to their respective weights.
2. You must satisfy **at least one** of the following two conditions:
   - **(a)** Obtain **50% or more** in the weighted average of Test #1 and Test #2 ($\ge 17.5 / 35.0$).
   - **(b)** Obtain **50% or more** in the Final Exam ($\ge 22.5 / 45.0$).

If you fail condition 2 despite having a weighted grade $\ge 50$, your recorded final grade will be capped at **47** (Auto-Fail).
:::

# Course Policies

*   **Generative Artificial Intelligence:** The use of generative AI tools or apps for any graded component in this course (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) is strictly prohibited.
*   **Academic Integrity:** Suspected cases of academic dishonesty will be investigated according to the University of Toronto's *Code of Behaviour on Academic Matters*.
*   **Absences & Missed Term Work:** There are no default makeup options for missed term work. Valid documented absences must be declared via ACORN and the DPES Missed Term Work Form. Missed test weights transfer to subsequent tests/exams.
*   **Classroom Etiquette:** Lectures and tutorials run from 12:10 pm to 2:00 pm. Electronic devices (phones, laptops, tablets) must be put away unless directly used for ongoing classroom tasks. No food or drinks permitted.
